reviews.weakest: 4 — “any computer,” “any AI,” “works the same way,” and “free for everyone” overstate what the linked implementation and limited 25-scenario test suite prove.
reviews.fix:
Insert immediately before
:

Before you start: You need internet access and a GitHub account with Copilot access. The installer supports current macOS, Windows 10/11 with winget, and Linux with apt or dnf. Memory files stay local, but recalled content is sent to Copilot to answer you. Shared or AI-generated agents are Python programs and may need review, fixes, or extra packages.

reviews.weakest: 6 (and 4): Step 4 and Step 5 tell a non-technical Mac user to use TextEdit and save an AI reply as a file ending in _agent.py, which in practice fails when TextEdit defaults to Rich Text (.rtf) or when the AI wraps code in markdown backticks.
reviews.fix:
In Step 5, make the creation step foolproof for non-technical users by replacing the span in
  • Make your own....
    • with: Paste that file into any AI and ask: "Write me a new agent just like this for [a chore you repeat] — give me only raw Python code with no markdown backticks, or a downloadable _agent.py file." Drag the plain-text _agent.py file onto your Brainstem window and it can use it on your next message.

reviews.weakest: 2: Brainstem, the thing the pasted command installs, is never defined outside the collapsed Details (its first visible use is step 1, after the command), and Terminal, PowerShell, Copilot and _agent.py are also unexplained, so a stranger cannot follow every word.
reviews.fix:
In the Start box replace

Open Terminal, paste this, press Enter.

with

This installs your Brainstem, the small program on your computer that runs your AI. On a Mac, press Cmd+Space, type Terminal and press Enter, then paste this and press Enter.

(MESSAGE.md's own definition, and it tells a first-timer how to reach Terminal.)
